boot.evidence: each round booted UML fresh (seccomp, 4 vCPU, 1 GiB) and reached its marker; the spread reflects payload weight (apt install and resize2fs inflate cap3/cap4, not the kernel)

i386_images.evidence: cap3 i386_run prints 'i686 I386_RUNS' for i386/alpine
i386_images.notes: the guest kernel still has CONFIG_COMPAT off (no native 32-bit); this is user-mode emulation registered through binfmt_misc, which the guest kernel does support

compose.evidence: two-service stack (web + worker with depends_on) came up, web logged STACK_WEB, down -v removed it

cgroup_cpu_limit.meaning: --cpus 0.5 -> cpu.max '50000 100000' read from inside the container

anon_rss_oom_kill.evidence: 64 MB-limited container killed with SIGKILL (137) while growing an anonymous buffer; the same allocator without a limit peaked at 153223168 bytes and kept running

tmpfs_not_charged.config: CONFIG_CGROUPS=y CONFIG_MEMCG=y # CONFIG_MEMCG_V1 is not set
tmpfs_not_charged.meaning: CONFIG_MEMCG=y but CONFIG_MEMCG_KMEM is absent, so tmpfs and page-cache pages are not charged to the container's cgroup: a 200 MB tmpfs write inside a 64 MB-limited container never approached the limit

cgroup_memory_limit.cgroup_path_note: the container cgroup lives at /sys/fs/cgroup/docker/<full-id> and is removed when the container exits (cap4 read it too late; cap5 read it while the container ran)

cgroup_io_limit.meaning: the cgroup v2 io controller exposes io.stat only; io.max is absent, so --device-*-bps limits cannot be enforced

ipv6_container_networking.ping_a_to_b: --- fd00:9::3 ping statistics --- 2 packets transmitted, 2 packets received, 0% packet loss round-trip min/avg/max = 1.426/1.758/2.090 ms
ipv6_container_networking.ping_b_to_a: --- fd00:9::2 ping statistics --- 2 packets transmitted, 2 packets received, 0% packet loss round-trip min/avg/max = 1.205/3.847/6.489 ms
ipv6_container_networking.evidence: two containers on a user-defined --ipv6 network ping each other over fd00:9::/64 with 0% loss both ways (avg 1.8 / 3.8 ms)
ipv6_container_networking.mechanism: dockerd logs 'Could not add route ... network is down' at network-create time because the bridge is still DOWN; the bridge comes UP when the first container attaches, and the container then receives its address and default route. The daemon error is cosmetic, not fatal.
ipv6_container_networking.refutes: the earlier claim 'IPv6 container networking does not work' (record 20261026-adv2b-corrected-probes.json, KNOWN-LIMITS.md)

ipv4_still_fine.evidence: 2 packets transmitted, 2 packets received, 0% packet loss round-trip min/avg/max = 92.575/94.855/97.135 ms

cap5.memcg_kmem_config: CONFIG_CGROUPS=y CONFIG_MEMCG=y # CONFIG_MEMCG_V1 is not set

known_limits_observed: no cgroup io.max: only io.stat exists; block-device limits are unenforceable
tmpfs and page cache are not charged to the cgroup (CONFIG_MEMCG_KMEM absent): memory limits only cap anonymous RSS
no native 32-bit userspace (CONFIG_COMPAT off); 32-bit images work only through qemu-user emulation registered in binfmt_misc
no cpuset controller: docker info still warns 'No cpuset support'
notes: Capability round 2 (cap3..cap6b) closes what round 1 left open: 32-bit images through qemu-user + binfmt_misc, a two-service Compose stack, BuildKit, the cpu and memory cgroup limits including a real OOM kill, and inter-container IPv6. It also retracts the earlier 'IPv6 does not work' claim: the daemon's route-add error at network creation is cosmetic -- the bridge comes UP when the first container attaches. Every value above is parsed from the raw console logs listed in artifacts; nothing is re-typed.
